title: The Three-Stage Pipeline
description: Keep the three stages of interpretation as separate, stateless functions: source to tokens, tokens to an AST, and AST plus environment to a value.

steps.description: This is the three-stage pipeline: source text becomes tokens, tokens become an AST, and the AST plus an environment becomes a value. The page calls keeping these stages as separate, stateless functions the most important architectural decision for testability.
`tokenize` turns source text into a list of tokens.
`parse` turns the token list into an AST, an abstract syntax tree.
`evaluate` takes the AST and an environment and returns a value.
`run` is a convenience entry point that chains all three: `evaluate(parse(tokenize(source)), Environment())`.

steps.question: The page says if each function is pure, with no global state and no mutation of shared objects, then every test is how many lines?
